symptoms: Olive-green to black, velvety spots on leaves.
Leaves may yellow and drop prematurely.
Scabby, dark, corky spots on fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_treatment: Apply fungicides containing captan, myclobutanil, or mancozeb early in the season.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_remedy: Use sulfur-based sprays or neem oil. Ensure good air circulation by pruning.
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves to reduce overwintering fungi.
Plant scab-resistant apple varieties.
Prune trees to improve air circulation and sunlight penetration.
Apple___Apple_scab.weather_precautions: Fungus thrives in cool, wet spring weather.

symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots: purple spots with tan centers.
Brown to black rot on fruit, often with concentric rings.
Cankers on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.organic_remedy: Remove and destroy infected plant parts (mummies, cankers, dead wood).
prevention: Prune out dead or diseased wood during the dormant season.
Remove mummified fruit.
Maintain tree vigor.
Apple___Black_rot.weather_precautions: Infection often occurs during warm, wet weather.

symptoms: Pale yellow spots on the upper surface of leaves that turn orange.
Orange, tube-like structures on the underside of leaves.
Yellow-orange spots on fruit.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.chemical_treatment: Fungicides like myclobutanil applied during the pink bud to petal fall stages.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.organic_remedy: Remove nearby eastern red cedar trees (the alternate host).
prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties.
Remove alternate hosts within a 1-2 mile radius if possible.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.weather_precautions: Spores spread during wet spring weather.

symptoms: None. Leaves are uniformly green and healthy.
prevention: Continue regular watering and fertilization schedules.
Maintain good orchard hygiene.

symptoms: Small, powdery, cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Leaves may yellow and dry out.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.chemical_treatment: Fungicides containing strobilurins or triazoles if infection is severe early in the season.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids.
Crop rotation may slightly help, though spores blow in from warmer regions.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.weather_precautions: Thrives in cool (16-25°C) and humid weather.

symptoms: None. Plant is healthy.
prevention: Maintain standard agricultural practices.

symptoms: Dark brown to black spots on older leaves with concentric rings (target-board appearance).
Lower leaves yellow and drop off.
Potato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb applied preventatively.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_remedy: Copper-based fungicides. Improve airflow and avoid overhead watering.
prevention: Practice 3-4 year crop rotation.
Remove and destroy infected plant debris.
Ensure plants are well-fertilized to reduce stress.
Potato___Early_blight.weather_precautions: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) alternating with wet/dry periods favor the disease.

symptoms: Water-soaked, pale green to dark brown spots on leaves.
White fungal growth on the underside of leaves in wet conditions.
Tubers develop dark, reddish-brown, dry rot.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans) - The cause of the Irish Potato Famine
Potato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Systemic fungicides like mefenoxam or chlorothalonil. Urgent application needed.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_remedy: Copper sprays can offer preventative protection. Destroy infected plants immediately.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed potatoes.
Destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles.
Hilling soil up around the base of plants protects tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.weather_precautions: Cool, wet, and humid weather drives rapid spread.

symptoms: None.
prevention: Maintain good crop rotation and watering practices.

symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves.
Spots may have a yellow halo.
Scab-like lesions on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.organic_remedy: Remove infected leaves. Avoid overhead watering.
prevention: Use disease-free seed and transplants.
Practice crop rotation (do not plant tomatoes or peppers in the same spot for 2-3 years).
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.weather_precautions: Spreads rapidly during periods of high moisture and warm temperatures.

symptoms: Dark, concentric rings on older leaves.
Leaves turn yellow and fall off.
Dark, leathery lesions at the stem end of fruit.
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_remedy: Neem oil or copper fungicides. Mulch around base of plants.
prevention: Remove lower leaves to prevent soil splash.
Stake or cage plants for better airflow.
Tomato___Early_blight.weather_precautions: Favored by warm temperatures and high humidity/frequent rain.

symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems.
White fuzzy growth on undersides of leaves.
Firm, dark brown, greasy spots on fruit.
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Fungicides like chlorothalonil. Apply at first sign of disease.
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_remedy: Copper fungicides. Destroy infected plants immediately.
prevention: Ensure good air circulation.
Avoid overhead watering.
Tomato___Late_blight.weather_precautions: Cool, wet nights and warm, humid days.

symptoms: None.
prevention: Maintain standard care.
